title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
synopsis: A cursed family, a monstrous hound and the fog-bound Devon moor. Holmes and Watson race to learn who, or what, is hunting the heir.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: London, on a foggy autumn night. In the rooms at 221B Baker Street, Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson are about to receive a most unusual visitor.

scenes.speaker: mortimer
scenes.text: Mr. Holmes, I come from Devonshire, where my friend Sir Charles Baskerville has died. The villagers say an ancient curse killed him. I need your advice.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Mortimer unrolled a yellowed manuscript. Three hundred years ago, it said, a cruel squire named Hugo Baskerville chased a young woman across the moor on a stormy night.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Hugo was found dead the next morning. And over his body, the shepherds swore, stood a giant black hound with eyes of fire.

scenes.speaker: mortimer
scenes.text: Since that day the family has been haunted. Three nights ago I found Sir Charles dead on the path. Beside his body, Mr. Holmes, were the footprints of an enormous hound.

scenes.speaker: holmes
scenes.text: Watson, I am needed in London, but you shall go. Travel to Baskerville Hall with the new heir, Sir Henry. Watch everything, and report to me every day.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: So the next day a train carried Dr. Watson and Sir Henry west, toward a land of mist, bog and secrets.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The carriage rolled across the moor as the sun sank low. Watson had never seen land so empty or so wild. Somewhere ahead stood Baskerville Hall.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The driver warned them of the Grimpen Mire, a bog that could swallow a pony whole, and of Selden, a dangerous convict who had escaped from Princetown prison.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Inside, the Hall was vast and cold. Portraits of long-dead Baskervilles stared down from the walls. That night, Watson woke to a sound he could not place.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: It was the sound of someone sobbing, quietly, somewhere deep in the house.

scenes.speaker: stapleton
scenes.text: I am a naturalist, Doctor. I collect butterflies on the moor. But take care. If you ever hear a strange howling at night, do not go out to find it.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: That night, from the mist, came a long, low howl. Watson stood frozen. It sounded like no animal he had ever heard.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Then he saw it. A tall figure stood on a distant tor, black against the moon. Watson could not tell whether it was a friend or an enemy.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Watson followed the figure to a stone hut among the rocks. Inside he found a bed, a lamp, and a note with his own name on it. He waited in the dark, gun in hand.

scenes.speaker: holmes
scenes.text: Good evening, Watson. I have been on this moor for days, watching. I believe I know who sent that hound. And tonight, I mean to catch him.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Holmes had solved it. The villain was Mr. Stapleton, a secret Baskerville cousin who wanted the family fortune. His weapon was a huge dog, painted to glow in the dark.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: That night, as planned, Sir Henry walked home across the moor. Holmes and Watson crouched among the rocks, waiting. The fog was rolling in.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Then came the howl. The hound burst out of the fog, huge and burning, racing straight toward Sir Henry.

scenes.speaker: holmes
scenes.text: Fire, Watson! Both men fired at once. The beast fell, and the glow died. It was only a dog, painted with phosphorus.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Stapleton fled into the Grimpen Mire, and the bog swallowed him. The curse was broken. Back at Baker Street, Holmes lit his pipe and smiled.
